qolFindings.title: Unused raw and read APIs remain outside the in-lock write guard
qolFindings.evidence: src/persistence/writeGuard.ts:94-100 reads compatibility before executeRaw acquires its write lease. get/getAll/getOptional still accept arbitrary SQL. The application has no mutating calls through these APIs; src/persistence/writeStatements.test.ts checks statement shapes rather than the execution method. This existing finding is recorded in docs/working/BACKLOG.md:222.
qolFindings.reproduction: Code inspection of the existing escape paths. The real-engine scratch probe confirms executeRaw now refuses a previously unmarked older instance after a newer claim. Its residual race and mutating SQL through read APIs remain the previously reported limitation.

roundTwoRecheck.evidence: VACUUM now executes through guarded writeLock without a transaction. The focused compaction test passed on Chromium and WebKit. Visible UI erase probes removed every IndexedDB block containing the synthetic marker, left freelist_count at zero and remained erased after reload. The final bounded WebKit replay passed on the frozen reviewed checkpoint.
03_TECHNICAL_DECISIONS.md §3.1 now requires the sync release to retain local-only tables under other view names until migration copies their rows, then remove them in a later release.

The contract documents that a failed open retains its claim. Unit coverage checks the failure ordering. Real-engine probes on both engines preserved version 0.7.0/minimum writer 0.6.0 after a throwing migration, wrote no migration ledger entry and refused the next 0.5.0 open's save.

The build validator calls parseVersion and encodeVersion. On the frozen checkpoint, regular 0.3.7 and test 0.4.7 were accepted; patch 1000, prerelease strings and different minor versions were refused for both channels.
03_TECHNICAL_DECISIONS.md §3.1 records that future read-only downloading must allow PowerSync's own subscription writes.
